patch_description:
The weakest metric is noise_reduction (0.33) with smoothness at 0.45, while correlation (0.79) and lag (0.43) have headroom to trade. Rather than touching the co-swept window/tilt pair (known to interact destructively), I strengthen the zero-phase noise-attacking stages that add no group delay:

1. `_median_snap` (Stage 3.5): currently blends sub-noise samples 50/50 with the local median only when steps fall below 0.5σ. I make the blend graded — closer to the noise floor gets a stronger pull toward the median (up to 0.75), and raise the trigger threshold to 0.7σ. Median filtering is edge-preserving, so genuine monotonic trends (whose steps are systematic, not sub-noise relative to local σ) pass untouched; this specifically removes residual fine-scale jitter after the SG stage, boosting noise_reduction and smoothness without adding phase delay.

2. `ZeroPhasePolishStage` (Stage 6): widen the symmetric SG polish from 7 to 9 taps. A zero-phase FIR adds no lag; a quadratic fit over 9 taps still tracks the 0.5 Hz–5 Hz components of the test signal well, but attenuates residual high-frequency variance further, directly attacking noise_reduction and reducing spurious slope sign flips (false_reversals, slope_changes).

Both edits are zero-phase, so lag_error and responsiveness_score should be unaffected while noise_reduction, smoothness_score, and reversal counts improve.
